note: Track sevenths-up, step 5 (maj7, 7 and m7): one ear game narrowed with qualities to the three chords the step names, the two notes that tell them apart said before the first answer, each answer named as the game's button shows it, and the goal an answer that comes at once. exercise.title: Name maj7, 7 and m7 by ear
exercise.why: The 7th sits a half step below the root's octave in maj7 and a whole step below it in 7 and m7, and only m7 has a minor 3rd, so two notes are enough to name any of the three.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below to hear a chord. Pick its kind: Major 7 for maj7, Dominant 7 for the chord written 7 (as in A7), or Minor 7 for m7.
Listen to the top note first: a half step below the root's octave means Major 7, a whole step below it means Dominant 7 or Minor 7. For those two, listen to the 3rd: a minor 3rd means Minor 7.
Press Replay in the game to hear the same chord again, and hum its top note.
Practice until the answer comes from the sound at once, without working it out note by note.
